text: Elijah stood on Mount Carmel with a nation watching.
The people had been pulled between God and Baal for too long.
Elijah called them to choose, and this day would make the truth plain.
Mount Carmel was full of people, noise, and waiting.
The prophets of Baal had come in great number.
Elijah stood before them as the prophet of God.
He looked alone, but he was not afraid.
The God who answered by fire would be God.
Two altars would be prepared, one for Baal and one for God.
The prophets would call on Baal, and Elijah would call on God.
The people could watch, listen, and decide whom they would follow.
The prophets of Baal went first.
They prepared the sacrifice and called on Baal from morning until noon.
But the altar stayed cold.
The prophets kept calling, but nothing happened.
They moved around the altar again.
Again, desperate for some sign that Baal could hear them.
They shouted louder, but louder did not make him real.
Baal did not answer.
The people had seen enough to understand what noise could not do.
A crowd can shout, and priests can perform with great energy.
The mountain was waiting for the true God.
Then Elijah called the people near.
He repaired the broken altar of God, stone by stone, while the people watched.
Now it was being restored.
Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe of Israel.
He was not inventing a new way.
He was calling the people back to the God who had already claimed them.
He prepared the sacrifice and laid it on the wood.
If fire came now, it would be God's fire.
Elijah stepped forward to pray.
He did not shout like the prophets of Baal.
The mountain grew still.
Then the fire of God fell.
It came from heaven and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the dust.
God had spoken with fire.
The people fell on their faces.
They could not stand in the middle anymore.
Baal had not answered, and God had answered in front of them all.
They cried out that God was God.
The living God had answered.
The mountain was no longer waiting.
The test was over, the fire had fallen.
The fire fell, and the lie broke.
